    Which hip turns the head
    
        
    In the CAD the head crank sits on the hip the CAD calls L1. You said R2 turns the head, which matches your labels being the CAD's turned 180°. Pick the one that matches your wiring.
    
        
        
        
    
        
    Head drive servo: 
    
      
    
      
    
        
    Calibration
    
        
    Angle each servo is at in the CAD drawing, and whether it turns the other way. Defaults: legs as drawn = stand; head as drawn = 90/90. If a joint moves the wrong way on screen compared with the robot, tick reverse.
    
        
    
        
    
      
    
      
    
        
    How the twin works
    
        
    Legs: each hip turns its femur about the servo shaft; each knee turns the foot and its servo about the femur's knee axis. Head yaw: the hip pin rides in the crank's 81° arc slot (dead zone), then pushes the crank, whose pin turns the turntable through its radial slot. Head pitch and roll: the neck pivots on the tower and the beam pivots on the neck; both rods are solved so they keep their length. The robot sits on its lowest point; balance and tipping are not simulated.
